originalTitle: Trump’s ballroom construction can resume at White House, supreme court rules – live
summary: In a 5-4 decision, the court granted the Trump administration’s request to block a lower court ruling that would have prevented work from being done on the ballroom
content: Former Colorado elections clerk Tina Peters, who was convicted in 2024 in relation to a plot to chase pro-Trump election conspiracies, has declined an offer to serve as an election consultant in a Northern California county, according to the Record Searchlight. Shasta County Registrar Clint Curtis caused widespread political backlash in recent weeks after he offered Peters a role as consultant, despite her election denial views and past conviction. California Governor Gavin Newsom on Monday vowed to block the hiring by instructing the state’s department of correction to reject the transfer of her parole supervision from Colorado. “Shasta County’s job offer to a felon CONVICTED OF TAMPERING WITH VOTING MACHINES to work on their election process is a disgrace,” Newsom’s press office posted on X. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down from his post after 18 months on the job and amid a wider shakeup of military leaders. Driscoll, a former Yale Law School classmate of JD Vance, submitted his resignation this week after months of tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, according to The Wall Street Journal. Hegseth has fired numerous top military leaders over the past year, including Army Chief of Staff Randy George. Driscoll was tasked last year with being the US government’s point person in negotiations between Russia and Ukraine in attempt to end their conflict, despite having little background in international diplomacy. He also backed incorporating more advanced technologies into the armed forces, including a push to cut down the time frame for testing new military technology. Donald Trump posted a Truth Social message on Monday evening celebrating the supreme court’s decision to allow construction to continue on his White House ballroom project. “I am pleased to report that the United States Supreme Court has just ruled in favor of the Ballroom/Military Complex being built without any further contingency, doubt, or threat,” Trump said. “We are living in the Golden Age of America, and this Building will be one of the Greatest ever constructed in Washington, D.C.” The supreme court’s decision to allow Donald Trump to continue with construction of his White House found that the group suing to block it did not have standing to bring its case. The 5-4 decision, backed by the conservative justices, ruled that the National Trust for Historic Preservation did not have legal standing and had not suffered “injury in fact” from the project. Chief Justice John Roberts, joined by liberal justices Elena Kagan, Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson, issued a dissenting opinion arguing that the court’s decision hands the presidency even more executive power and that the ballroom’s construction is likely unlawful. “The president ordered the demolition of the East Wing of the White House to make way for a new, privately funded state ballroom in its place. Construction of the ballroom has proceeded apace for the better part of a year,” Chief Justice John Roberts wrote in a dissent. “That construction is likely unlawful”. The Supreme Court issued a decision on Monday that gives Donald Trump the ability to proceed with his plans for construction of a new White House ballroom. Trump’s plans for a White House ballroom have been an ongoing point of contention and legal action, with opponents arguing that Trump has no legal authority to pursue the project without congressional approval. In a 5-4 decision, the court granted the Trump administration’s request to block a lower court ruling that would have prevented work from being done on the ballroom. The Supreme Court also issued a temporary order earlier this month which allowed work to continue on the ballroom, resulting in Democratic Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer accusing the court of “rubber stamping Trump’s vanity-driven, gilded corruption”. In the Oval Office today, Donald Trump said the latest strikes on Iran, as the two countries exchange fire for the first time in a month, are part of a “limited” campaign. “They’re a failed nation,” the president said after threatening to hit “Iran” hard after the regime struck Jordanian airbases over the weekend. “Their leaders are largely dead. Their navy is gone. Their air force is gone,” Trump told reporters today. “That doesn’t mean we won’t smack them. We’ll see what happens.” The president also claimed that traffic is increasing through the vital strait of Hormuz chokepoint, even though the average number is substantially lower – and has remained so – since the war began. There was, however, an uptick in the number of transits in the past two weeks, before the most recent strikes. Chris Hippensteel Vance – who has now finished speaking in Michigan – also fired back at El-Sayed for comments the Democratic nominee made about Vance’s wife on social media. “Abdul, keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth because she’s way out of your league,” Vance told the crowd. El-Sayed had previously insinuated in a post that Vance would not have introduced his wife, Usha, to his late grandfather, a remark that was widely interpreted as jab at Usha Vance’s Indian-American heritage. Donald Trump is now speaking in the Oval Office about price cuts for prescription drugs. We’ll bring you the latest lines. Chris Hippensteel JD Vance has turned his address in Michigan toward Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Mike Rogers’ Democratic opponent in Michigan’s Senate race. The vice-president is taking aim at El-Sayed’s association with leftwing political commentator Hasan Piker, and for comments El-Sayed made after an attack on the Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield, Michigan, in March. El-Sayed has apologized for those comments, saying they were meant to add context. chineseTitle: 最高法院规定，特朗普的宴会厅建设可以在白宫恢复——现场直播
chineseSummary: 法院以 5 比 4 的投票结果批准了特朗普政府的请求，阻止下级法院做出一项阻止舞厅工作的裁决。
